Adds a fixed 30-second deadline to Google Chat’s google-auth guarded fetch transport and updates three focused transporter expectations.

PR surface: Source +2, Tests +3. Total +5 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. with high confidence from source: current google-auth requests enter fetchWithSsrFGuard without a deadline, and the controlled hanging-proxy proof shows the patched production path now terminates near 30 seconds. The focused test also verifies exact option forwarding.

target.title: fix(googlechat): bound auth transporter fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Chat's direct API calls already run through a 30-second guarded-fetch timeout, but the google-auth transport used before those API calls did not pass a timeout into the same guard. A stalled token or certificate fetch could therefore hang the outbound/verification path before the existing Google Chat API timeout was reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the plugin-owned google-auth transport on the same bounded network contract as the rest of the Google Chat channel. The change is intentionally narrow: it only passes the existing 30-second deadline into `fetchWithSsrFGuard` for google-auth requests and updates focused tests to assert that option forwarding.

## User Impact

Google Chat auth network stalls now fail with the existing guarded-fetch timeout instead of waiting indefinitely. Normal auth endpoint responses still flow through the same transport.

## Evidence

Current pushed head: `4d11d2880d511fcfbe8d2403f5def5fe0e9edabc`.

Duplicate preflight before opening found no existing public issue or PR occupying this exact hidden bug:

```text
$ gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --match title,body --limit 50 --json number,title,state,url,updatedAt -- "google chat auth transporter timeout"
[]
$ gh search issues --repo openclaw/openclaw --match title,body --limit 50 --json number,title,state,url,updatedAt -- "google chat auth transporter timeout"
[]
$ gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --match title,body --limit 50 --json number,title,state,url,updatedAt -- "google-auth fetch timeout googlechat"
[]
$ gh search issues --repo openclaw/openclaw --match title,body --limit 50 --json number,title,state,url,updatedAt -- "google-auth fetch timeout googlechat"
[]
```

Focused regression test on the rebased head:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-messaging.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/codex/openclaw


 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
   Start at  20:08:24
   Duration  15.28s (transform 11.94s, setup 1.62s, import 48ms, tests 13.27s, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 20.92s
```

Whitespace/diff sanity on the rebased head:

```text
$ git diff --check
```

Controlled runtime proof using the real `createGoogleAuthFetch()` and a local hanging proxy. The request is an actual google-auth token URL request routed through the production guarded fetch path; the proxy accepts the TCP connection and never answers, so the only successful result is the production timeout firing near 30 seconds:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --eval '<controlled stalled proxy script using createGoogleAuthFetch()>'
[stalled-auth] proxy=http://127.0.0.1:34071
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 30000ms (elapsed 30003ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=https://oauth2.googleapis.com/***
[stalled-auth] elapsedMs=30212 name=TimeoutError message=request timed out
```

Normal endpoint proof using the same real `createGoogleAuthFetch()` with no secrets. The Google token endpoint returns its expected invalid-request response instead of being broken by the transport change:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --eval '<normal createGoogleAuthFetch token endpoint script>'
[normal-auth] elapsedMs=504 status=400
[normal-auth] bodyPrefix={ "error": "unsupported_grant_type", "error_description": "Invalid grant
```

Autoreview tooling was attempted before the earlier push but unavailable in this environment:

```text
$ .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local
codex engine failed (1)

$ .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude --no-tools --no-web-search
executable not found: claude

$ .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine pi --no-web-search
executable not found: pi
```
